content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list: 168.30, 130.70,130.27,128.35,126.66,124.85,123.57,58.70,36.40,36.40,26.40.

We need number of methyl (CH3) groups in the molecule. Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but also 20-30 for typical. Here we have peaks at 58.70 (likely O-CH3), 36.40 (two identical), 26.40. The 58.70 could be a methoxy carbon (O-CH3). 36.40 could be CH2 or CH3 attached to something. 26.40 likely CH3. Need to deduce number of methyl groups.

We also have aromatic carbons (130-124). 168 carbonyl.

Methyl groups: each CH3 carbon gives a signal. So count distinct methyl carbon signals. 58.70 is a methyl attached to O (methoxy). 26.40 is a methyl likely attached to alkyl. 36.40 could be CH2 (but chemical shift for CH2 is ~30-40). But there are two identical signals at 36.40, could be two equivalent CH2 groups or two equivalent CH3? CH3 attached to something like carbonyl (acetyl) appears ~30. So ambiguous.

We could use HSQC to see which are CH3 vs CH2. Let's get HSQC.
